name: watchman-tower
description: Check website, server, SSL and domain monitoring in Watchman Tower, review incidents and response times, and add, pause or resume monitors.

interface.longDescription:
Watchman Tower monitors websites, servers, SSL certificates and domains, and alerts your team when something breaks. This connector brings your Watchman Tower account into the conversation.

Ask for a health overview, find monitors that are down or slow, look at recent incidents and what caused them, check response time trends, see which certificates or domains expire soon, and review CPU, memory and disk usage on servers running the Watchman Tower agent.

If you allow it on the consent screen, the assistant can also add new monitors, pause and resume monitors, and delete monitors. Deletion is never immediate: a deleted monitor is paused and kept for 7 days, and can be restored from chat or the dashboard during that time.

The connector sees exactly what you see in the dashboard, including team and shared monitors. Every request uses the same permissions, plan limits and rate limits as the Watchman Tower public API. Read access is granted when you connect; write access is opt-in. You can disconnect at any time from API Keys → Connected apps.

Requires a Watchman Tower account on a plan with API access (Team or Stack).
capabilities: Read monitor status, incidents, response times and server metrics
Add, pause, resume, delete and restore monitors when allowed
defaultPrompt: Is everything OK with my sites?
Show the incidents from the last 24 hours and what caused them.
Which SSL certificates or domains expire soon?

positive.prompt: Give me an overview of my monitors.
positive.expected_behavior: Summarizes monitor counts by state, open incidents and active conditions.

positive.prompt: Which of my monitors are down right now?
positive.expected_behavior: Lists monitors that are down or degraded, or says none are.
Lists open incidents with monitor name, start time and cause.

positive.prompt: Which certificates or domains are close to expiry?
positive.expected_behavior: Lists SSL certificates and domains that expire soon with their dates.

positive.prompt: Add an HTTPS monitor for https://www.iana.org named IANA.
positive.expected_behavior: Asks for confirmation, creates the monitor and returns its name and URL.

negative.description: Monitoring infrastructure the user does not own

Change my Watchman Tower billing plan to Stack.

publication.release_notes: First release: read monitors, incidents, conditions, status pages and server stats; add, pause, resume, delete and restore monitors with opt-in write access.
